question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to register and reuse global stdio MCP declarations, and if so, what host-controlled authorization and command-broker contract is required?
rationale: The branch intentionally introduces a new cross-Claw ownership and local-process execution model; source review cannot choose the product security boundary on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Require brokered and host-authorized MCPs
options.body: Accept only host-brokered or allowlisted stdio commands and require explicit host authorization before sharing or reusing a global MCP declaration.

options.title: Scope declarations per Claw
options.body: Use Claw-scoped MCP identities so exact declarations cannot be silently shared across agents or installations.

options.title: Pause this stage
options.body: Defer MCP lifecycle support until the RFC defines the execution and shared-resource authorization model.

recommendation.title: Require brokered and host-authorized MCPs
recommendation.body: Accept only host-brokered or allowlisted stdio commands and require explicit host authorization before sharing or reusing a global MCP declaration.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the PR and have already reviewed the lifecycle/configuration boundary in detail.
